title: Hourly burn to latency: pricing & HC probe (Q2 2026)
content:
Executive summary:

This worksheet explores the coupling between hourly cash burn, expected latency SLOs, and price-per-1k-token sensitivity for our hosted API SKU. Purpose is to provide a short-cycle headcount + pricing playbook for a 12-week sprint window (Q2 2026) with three scenarios: baseline (steady growth), high-throughput (adoption spike), and constrained-capacity (GPU shortage).

Core questions: 
- If we need to tighten latency SLO from p95=120ms -> p95=80ms, what is the incremental hourly cost (ops + infra + hiring) and what price delta do we need to keep margin stable?
- What are near-term headcount trades (contractor vs perm) that change burn profile quickly?
- Which pricing sensitivity bands materially change take-rate and net margin under each scenario?

Key assumptions (explicit):
- Hosted API baseline traffic: 12M tokens/day (mix: 70% gen, 30% embeddings/others)
- Average tokens per request: 300
- Baseline infra footprint: 18 dedicated GPU cards across regions for hosted capacity; baseline GPU cost (cloud + infra) = $28/hr per card (effective after committed discounts)
- Ops/overhead burden (monitoring, autoscaling, SRE rotations) = $7k/mo (alloc to hosted line)
- Average loaded headcount cost (total comp + burden) per FTE = $220k/year -> $18.3k/mo -> hourly ~ $105 (assuming 40h/wk) (used for quick on-call costing)
- Contractor hourly fully-burdened = $120/hr
- Average onboarding one L3 infra engineer (perm) takes 8 weeks to hit velocity; contractor 2 weeks to 70% velocity
- Price per 1k tokens (current list): $0.60 per 1k gen tokens, $0.12 per 1k embeddings (blended current revenue per 1k tokens = $0.48)

Quick baseline math (summary):
- Tokens/day 12M -> 360M tokens/mo ~ 360 * (1k) = 360k *1k tokens/mo
- Monthly revenue (baseline blended) = 360k * $0.48 = $172.8k/mo
- Monthly infra burn: 18 cards * 24hr * 30days * $28 = $362,880/mo (note: this includes shared infra for other workloads; allocate 35% to hosted API -> $126,008/mo)
- Ops & headcount allocation to hosted API: 2.5 FTEs equivalent -> 2.5 * $18.3k = $45.8k/mo
- Net (before other OpEx) = Revenue $172.8k - Infra alloc $126.0k - Ops $45.8k = approx $1k/mo (near break-even currently).

This baseline is deliberately tight to illustrate sensitivity — small changes to price or capacity materially affect margin.

Scenario sensitivity table (high level) — the sheet contains more granular tabs but summarized here:

ASCII table (rounded numbers):
| Scenario                | Token/mo (M) | Revenue/mo | Infra alloc/mo | Ops & HC/mo | Net/mo  | Notes                              |
|------------------------|--------------:|-----------:|---------------:|-----------:|--------:|-------------------------------------|
| Baseline               | 360           | $172.8k    | $126.0k        | $45.8k     | $1.0k   | current mix, p95=120ms              |
| Adoption spike (+50%)  | 540           | $259.2k    | $189.0k        | $52.0k     | $18.2k  | need burst cards (50% more)         |
| Lower latency (p95 80) | 360           | $172.8k    | $172.0k        | $62.0k     | -$61.2k | more cards + routing + SRE oncall   |
| Capacity shock (-30%)  | 252           | $121.0k    | $88.2k         | $45.8k     | -$12.9k | spot price increase + queueing      |

Notes on the lower-latency row: to drop p95 from 120ms to 80ms we estimated +36% infra (more reserved on hot shards, lower packing density) and +35% ops overhead (dedicated on-call, runbooks, prewarming). That drives the heavy negative net.

Pricing sensitivity: break-even price computation (for baseline):
- To recover incremental cost of lower-latency change (+Infra $46k/mo + +Ops $16.2k/mo = ~$62.2k/mo), we can: increase price per 1k tokens, add SLO premium (flat add-on), or try to reduce headcount/onboarding time via contractors.
- Required blended price uplift = incremental_cost / token_k_units = $62.2k / 360k = $0.173 per 1k tokens.
- Baseline blended price = $0.48 -> Break-even blended = $0.48 + $0.173 = $0.653 per 1k tokens (~+36%).

Price band sensitivity (illustrative):
- If list price raised by +20% -> blended becomes $0.576 -> Revenue/mo = 360k * $0.576 = $207.4k -> Net = $207.4k - $126.0k - $45.8k = $35.6k
- If list price raised by +36% -> blended $0.653 -> Revenue/mo = $235.1k -> Net = $63.3k (covers latency uplift)
- If price raised +50% -> blended $0.72 -> Revenue/mo = $259.2k -> Net = $87.4k

Demand elasticity notes (back-of-envelope):
- Historical demand vs price elasticity: -0.8 at aggregate (we've observed 5% revenue drop from 10% price increase in certain slabs). For hosted API mid-market customers elasticity likely lower (-0.5) for small increases; high-elasticity accounts are low-value, high-volume experimental users.
- Using elasticity -0.8, a +36% price hike could reduce tokens by ~28% -> new tokens=259M -> revenue = 259k * $0.653 = $169.1k -> net = $169.1k - $126.0k - $45.8k = -$2.7k (so not breakeven once elasticity is considered).

Headcount trade options (12-week window):
- Option A: Contractors x2 (4-week ramp to 70% velocity), cost ~ $120/hr * 40h * 4 = $19.2k each in month1 (front-loaded), reduces ops delta by 40% temporarily. Short-term burn spike but faster mitigation for latency incidents.
- Option B: Hire 1 perm L3 (+8-week ramp) cost ~$18.3k/mo loaded; longer-term cheaper but not useful within the 12-week sprint for immediate SLO changes.
- Option C: Reallocate platform SRE time from non-critical queues (internal re-prioritization) -> immediate but carries internal product risk and customer support load. Value = shifting 0.8 FTE (~$14.6k/mo) to hosted.

Short-cycle recommendation matrix (for exec decisions):
- If we must achieve p95 80ms within 12 weeks and keep customer-facing availability: combine Contractor x2 + temporary 20% price SLO premium (documented as "latency-pro">+20% to requests with SLO upgraded to 80ms). This reduces elasticity risk because premium can be targeted to enterprise customers who value latency.
- If tolerance for price moves is low: invest in medium-term commit to Dedicated pool (reserve capacity) and run a 6-week canary to shift heavy customers to dedicated offering (trade-off: lower margin but preserve hosted SLOs).

Operational checklist / actionable items (owners):
- Finance (Aisha) -> run detailed token-by-customer elasticity simulation within 72 hours (link model: Confluence PL-442) [Due: 2026-04-24]
- Infra (Marcus) -> provide exact infra delta plan for p95=80ms, include per-region card counts and prewarm cost [Due: 2026-04-23]
- Product (Sofia) -> draft SLO premium product page + billing SKU to test +20% latency premium for enterprise routes [Due: 2026-04-28]
- Sales -> identify top 20 customers by 30-day token volume for targeted pricing experiments and callouts [Due: 2026-04-25]

Back-of-envelope burn profile (first 8 weeks) for Contractor route:
Week 1: contractor onboarding costs & ramp -> +$38k burn (2 contractors), infra stable
Week 2-4: ops improvement kicks in, reduce incidents -> marginal infra efficiency up to 5% 
Week 5-8: measure latency p95 -> if improved -> roll down contractor use or switch to perm hire decision point

Open questions / unknowns:
- Precision of elasticity at slab boundaries vs blended aggregate; need per-customer A/B test to quantify.
- Contracting lead time and legal review needs (SOW template exists but confirm rate ceilings).
- Can Dedicated offering be used as buffer for top customers without cannibalizing host revenue?

Quick references / links:
- Confluence: PL-442 (token price probe)
- JIRA: JIRA-2468 (latency SLO infra work)
- GitHub infra PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/721 (prewarm change)

Notes to self (informal):
- This is intentionally conservative on infra effective cost (we assume $28/card/hr) — if reserved discounts deeper, the delta improves. Also caching and prefix sharing could salvage a lot of costs, need eng to provide prefix hit-rate scenarios.
- If we can identify high-volume customers who accept routing to dedicated for a small uplift, could avoid global price increases and preserve developer ecosystem usage.

Appendix: quick sample calculation snippets (for the main model tab):
- monthly_tokens_k = monthly_tokens / 1000
- required_price_uplift = incremental_cost / monthly_tokens_k
- elasticity_adjusted_tokens = monthly_tokens * (1 + price_delta * elasticity)
